sections.overview: Apistogramma similis is a small South American dwarf cichlid described by Wolfgang Staeck in 2003 from Bolivia. Its original locality is a forest brook beside Laguna La Brava in the río Yata system, within Beni Department.
sections.identification: The holotype measured 3.8 cm in standard length, but this single specimen is not a reliable adult maximum. FishBase gives no maximum or sex-specific length, mass, body width or height.
sections.habitat: The type specimen came from a forest stream at Laguna La Brava, but later records extend well beyond that single site. A survey near Santa Ana del Yacuma recorded the species in the río Mamoré subdrainage of the Bolivian Amazon.
sections.diet: A species-specific diet study was not found in the consulted references. It is safest to describe its feeding ecology as insufficiently documented rather than assign it a precise prey list from aquarium observations or genus-level assumptions.
sections.behavior: Direct observations of its behavior in the wild remain sparse in the available species accounts. Specialist cichlid records classify it as a harem-forming cave brooder, a useful reproductive pattern that should not be mistaken for a detailed field study.
sections.reproduction: The Cichlid Room Companion records substrate cave spawning and polygynous harem breeding for this species. Reliable field measurements of clutch size, incubation time and parental roles were not found in the consulted sources.
sections.ecology: The name similis means similar and refers to its close visual resemblance to the Bolivian A. inconspicua and A. linkei. The Cichlid Room places it in the regani group, so A. bitaeniata should not be assumed to be a close relative.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment lists Apistogramma similis as Least Concern, assessed on 23 April 2014 and published in 2016. The assessment and later records show a broader Bolivian lowland distribution than the original type locality alone suggests.
